sources.entry: ezbookkeeping - A lightweight personal bookkeeping app hosted by yourself. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: ezBookkeeping is a self-hosted, open-source personal finance and bookkeeping app for recording transactions, importing bank and accounting files, and analyzing spending with charts.
summary.what_it_does: It records daily income and expense transactions with two-level accounts and categories, image attachments, location tracking on maps, and scheduled transactions. Users can search, filter, and visualize bills, and build custom charts to analyze spending patterns. It imports CSV, Excel, OFX, QFX, QIF, IIF, Camt.052, Camt.053, MT940, GnuCash, Firefly III, and Beancount files, with custom column mapping, rules, and scripts for CSV and Excel. It supports multiple languages, currencies, timezones, and exchange rate sources with automatic updates. Security features include two-factor authentication, OIDC login, login rate limiting, and an application lock using PIN or WebAuthn. It also offers AI-assisted text and receipt image recognition, AI chart generation, and MCP integration, and is deployable via Docker (SQLite, MySQL, or PostgreSQL) or as a binary.
use_cases: track daily personal expenses and income
self-host a personal budgeting app on a home server or NAS
import bank statements into a bookkeeping app
analyze spending trends with custom charts
run personal finance tracking on a Raspberry Pi
use a finance app as a mobile PWA
how_to_run: ./ezbookkeeping server run (Linux / macOS / FreeBSD, from binary release)
notable: Runs on home servers, NAS, and Raspberry Pi with a single Docker command
Supports AI receipt and text recognition plus MCP integration for AI tools
Broad import support including Beancount, GnuCash, Firefly III, MT940, and Camt formats
Tailored mobile and desktop UIs with PWA installation
caveats: Production use requires mounting a persistent volume to prevent data loss, per the README
Building from source requires Golang, GCC, Node.js, and NPM installed
